messages:
sam: Hey @ryan @maya — PR #8427 is currently gated on the RFC (link below). Can we get an architecture check before I merge? Main questions: KV cache invalidation semantics across shards, and whether the fallback routing needs extra state. RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-kv-cache-sharding

maya: saw the PR, thanks for the ping. which routes will be affected most — router or frontend?

sam: mostly router + serving runtime. PR: https://git.redwood/team/redwood-inference/pull/8427 — changes are in runtime/cache_manager.go and the default config for cache_window. small snippet: ```go
// cache window ms
const CacheWindow = 50
```

ryan: I'll take a look today. quick ask: what's the expected change in p50/p95 token latency? also need a canary plan (duration, %).

sam: short answer: p50 ~ +1ms, p95 +6-8ms on long sequences (est from microbench). Canary plan I'm proposing: 5% traffic for 6h, then 25% for 24h if no regressions. I added perf bench screenshots in the PR comments.

jordan: tests passed for me locally. happy to coordinate the rollout once arch gives the go.

deploy-bot: CI passed — all checks green (build 8242). :white_check_mark:

ryan: two requests before I LGTM: 1) add a concise "Implementation details" subsection in the RFC summarizing shard key + invalidation flow, 2) add an integration test that simulates shard failover and verifies no stale KV hits. After that, ping me and I'll give architecture ack.

maya: also please loop in eng-sre for canary quota and alert hooks. @eng-sre-bot can you confirm standby/quota?

eng-sre-bot: tagged and noted. We'll validate canary quota and alert playbook by EOD.

sam: will update the RFC and add the integration test today, then ping here. thanks for the guidance.

ryan: great — also include the exact canary config snippet in the PR (percent + rollout window + abort thresholds). I want to be able to read the plan without switching between files. I'll aim to LGTM by EOD tomorrow once that's in.

sam: done — PR description updated with RFC link, short implementation summary, and canary steps. @ryan please review when you have a chance. :pray:
